transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Yeah, um… I came in because I’m not eating right anymore. Like, it’s gotten pretty bad. Some days I’ll realize I’ve only had coffee, and maybe a piece of bread or something small like that, and then the whole day’s gone.

And it’s not like I’m trying to lose weight or anything. My pants are actually hanging loose on me now, like I keep having to pull them up. I just… I don’t have much appetite, or I don’t get around to eating, and then when I think about food it feels like too much. So that’s what made me think maybe I should come talk to somebody, because it’s not normal for me.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… yeah, I have. Most days I wake up and it’s like there’s this heavy, empty feeling sitting right in my chest before I even really get out of bed. Like I open my eyes and there’s already this feeling of, I don’t know… nothing good is waiting for me. Nothing to look forward to.

It’s not just being tired or having a bad morning. It feels deeper than that, like I just want to keep my head down and get through the day without having to think too much or deal with anything. Even when nothing has happened yet, I already feel low, like the day is kind of ruined before it starts.
How long have you been feeling this way — this lack of appetite and the heavy, empty feeling in your chest?

It’s been… about five months, I think. Not just a couple bad weeks or anything like that. It’s been hanging over me for around five months now, the not eating right and that heavy, empty feeling.

At first I kind of thought maybe it would pass, like maybe I was just in a rough patch, but then it kept going. Days started blending together, and I’d keep thinking, “Okay, maybe tomorrow I’ll feel normal,” but it’s just stayed there. So yeah… about five months.
Have you ever had any periods where your mood felt unusually high or you had much more energy than usual, even if it was for just a few days?

Yeah… I think so. There was a time right after I got fired where I didn’t feel low like this. It was almost the opposite, honestly. I got this feeling like I was fired up, like nobody could really touch me or stop me. Like getting fired should’ve knocked me down, but instead I had this thing in my head like, “No, I’m fine, I’ll show everybody.”

And I remember people around me would say stuff like, “Maybe slow down a little,” or “Don’t get ahead of yourself,” and I’d get irritated really fast. Like, way faster than normal. I’d snap at them because it felt like they were trying to hold me back or talk down to me. At the time I didn’t really see it as a problem. I just thought I had energy and I was finally not taking crap from anybody. But looking back, yeah, it was kind of unusual for me.
How long did that unusually high mood last? Was it for just a day, a few days, or longer?

It wasn’t just one day. I wish it had been, because then maybe I could say it was just a reaction or just me trying to prove something after getting fired. But that whole swing — from feeling really driven and kind of unstoppable after I was fired, and then ending up down like this — it’s been going on for about a month.

It’s scary, honestly, because it doesn’t feel like my mood just changed a little. It feels like I got pulled way up in one direction and then dropped hard the other way. The high part was more than a day, more than just waking up with a burst of energy, and the whole thing has taken about a month from that fired-up feeling to where I am now.

During that time when you felt unusually high or fired up, did you ever feel like your thoughts were racing so much that it was hard to keep up, or that you were talking so fast other people had trouble following you?

Yeah… yeah, my thoughts were racing. It wasn’t just like normal worrying or thinking a lot. It was like my head was packed full of ideas all at the same time, and one thought would turn into another before I could even finish the first one.

Like I’d think, “Okay, I need a job,” and then suddenly that turned into some whole plan, and then that plan turned into another idea, and then another. It was like I couldn’t keep the pieces in order. I’d try to slow myself down, like tell myself, “Just focus on one thing,” but it wouldn’t really listen. My mind kept jumping ahead.

I don’t know how to explain it right, but it felt like my brain was running faster than I could keep up with. Like there were too many tabs open in my head, and they were all making noise at once. It was exhausting in a way, but at the time I also felt like those ideas were important, like I had to follow all of them right then.
